races.name: Download The At The Races App Selling Handicap

runners_data.name: Douglas Dc
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up specialist for Tony Carroll with AW form at this trip and similar going, placed twice over 1m2f-1m4f on Good; at 15 days since last run he should be fresh, though natural rear position is crowded in this field and he will need the clearest of passages.

runners_data.name: Cezarro
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon 4yo with AW placed form (2nd over 1m STA) and multiple AW starts suggesting course comfort; 37 days since last run is a slight query, and while his true style is wait-and-pounce, that role is congested here, meaning he may need a positive ride to matter.

runners_data.name: Heart Sign
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy booking is the headline angle for this Jack Morland 3yo; visor fitted and AW placed over 1m2f, he has the tactical jockey to navigate a sprint finish better than most in the field, though 10f is probably his optimum and 1m4f is a step up in trip.

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Robert Stephens runner with the best AW win record in the race (2W4P from 15 AW starts) and proven at this trip and going on multiple occasions; tongue strap fitted and OR=46 is competitive, making him the most credible beneficiary if the race is truly run at a crawl — his natural style is hold-up but trainer pace instructions could see him slot closer.

runners_data.name: Premier Cru
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe 3yo with tongue tie fitted and a trainer in decent 14-day form (4/16); AW placed over 1m2f STA but all form has been in defeat and OR=57 at this level suggests marginal ability, with no obvious tactical edge in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Maryland Star
runners_data.note: Dean Ivory 3yo flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a serious concern in a race that is overwhelmingly likely to be decided by a late sprint; hood fitted and AW placed at 1m2f, but the finishing-fade flag makes this shape the worst possible scenario for his chances.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Dream
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover 3yo also carrying the fade-in-finish flag, compounding concerns for a race shape that will demand a sustained burst late; unplaced in all AW starts and lowest OR in the field at 45, she is out of her comfort zone on trip and in a sprint scenario.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore 5yo carrying top weight of 140lbs, which is notable in a selling handicap; 2nd over 1m2f AW STA in recent form is directly relevant, and Rhys Clutterbuck has a 5/34 trainer strike rate — a genuine player if the sprint unfolds cleanly, though the weight burden is real over 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Lunar Power
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan 8yo wearing a hood and stepping back from extreme distances (placed 5th twice over 2m+ recently); Georgia Dobie rides and the horse's prior AW experience is solid, but the natural hold-up style is squeezed by the volume of closers here, and 49 days since last run adds freshness uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Cloud
runners_data.note: Second Dean Ivory runner in the race alongside Maryland Star; hood worn and AW placed (4th, 1m2f STA) with multiple AW outings suggesting track familiarity — Robert Havlin is a reliable AW jockey but the horse's recent finishing positions (9,5,4,7,8) paint a picture of a horse that threads quietly into modest positions rather than winning.

races.paceDynamic: Every runner in this 11-horse field is catalogued as a hold-up type, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and the race is almost certain to crawl early before exploding into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs at Lingfield's AW straight. With no horse genuinely willing to make the running, the pace will be manufactured rather than natural — likely a slow-motion procession through the first mile before the field concertinas and launches simultaneously, rewarding whoever can find the clearest passage and sustain a finish. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: horses with the most raw finishing speed and the best draw or widest passage to switch around the field will be at a premium, while horses that need genuine galloping conditions or a true stamina test will find this shape unflattering. The field holds more hold-up types than can physically come from the back in a sprint finish — Lunar Power, Maryland Star, Moonlit Cloud, and Sapphire Dream are among those most likely to be shuffled wider or earlier than ideal, with Heart Sign, Mister Daydream, and Marinakis marginally better positioned to punch through from a compact midfield in the final dash.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Strongest Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow throughout, the field bunches and the race becomes a 2f dash from the home bend.
scenarios.body: The compact finish suits whoever can find a clear run earliest from midfield; Heart Sign (Oisin Murphy, strong tactical rider) and Mister Daydream (prior AW placed form) are best equipped to accelerate in a sprint. Horses with any stamina-over-speed bias will be flattered by the distance but beaten by the clock.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Emerges Cheap
scenarios.trigger: If one horse breaks the pattern and nudges forward unchallenged to steal a soft lead at a steady tempo.
scenarios.body: With no natural front-runner, any horse willing to slot in front and control fractions could dictate entirely and never face a true challenge until the last furlong. Marinakis (has won on AW, placed multiple times at this trip and going) is the likeliest beneficiary if connections elect to alter tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Wide Draw Wins
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems develop at the sprint stage and the widest or most patient travellers get the cleaner passage.
scenarios.body: A field of 11 true hold-up types fanning wide around Lingfield's final bend regularly produces scrimmaging; horses drawn or ridden wide, like Lunar Power or Cezarro who has AW placed form, can benefit by bypassing the carnage inside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens early — perhaps through a false start or early jostling — turning this into a genuine test of staying power.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop over 1m4f on AW Standard would expose those lacking stamina and reward horses that have been running over longer trips; Douglas Dc (placed twice over this distance at Good) and Mister Daydream (2nd over 10f AW) would cope best.

watchPoints.text: Maryland Star and Sapphire Dream are both flagged as horses that fade in the finish — in a race almost certain to be decided by a sprint, monitor their market moves late: drifting odds would confirm the pace scenario that kills their chance entirely.

With 10 true hold-up types launching simultaneously at the home bend, watch for severe traffic problems inside the final 2f — horses drawn low or trapped on the rail at that point (particularly in a bunched field of 11) risk being seriously hampered or checked.

Mister Daydream carries 140lbs — the top weight in a selling handicap — and his chance deteriorates sharply if the race develops any genuine galloping pace rather than the expected sprint; monitor how freely he travels in the first mile.

Oisin Murphy on Heart Sign is the most significant jockey-horse pairing in the race given the tactical nature of the contest — if Murphy elects to position earlier than the horse's natural style would suggest, it could fundamentally alter the complexion of the sprint finish.

Marinakis has the strongest AW winning profile in the field (2W from 15 AW starts, multiple places) and if Robert Stephens instructs Luke Morris to take a slightly more forward position than usual, the horse's course-and-distance record makes it a meaningful threat across multiple scenarios.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 1)
Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 2)
Syd Renwick 90th Birthday Handicap

runners_data.name: Artavian
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner who sets every tactical parameter in this race; recent form of 992-73 is modest at this level but the ability to dictate an uncontested gallop on a track and surface it has form on (sim-going 8/15 with two places) is a significant compensating factor, even if the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations slightly.

runners_data.name: Master Dancer
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose form at Lingfield over 1m4f-1m6f includes a third place on Standard; a natural deep closer by style, though the crowded hold-up division means it is unlikely to get clean daylight from the rear, and recent form of 0-9630 does not inspire confidence at OR 52.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Strong staying profile with a genuine win over 2m on Standard ground (1/16f/STA) just seven days ago — fitness is not a concern; a true hold-up runner who will need to find room in a congested rear pack, but the proven trip and surface give it the clearest credentials of any closer in this field.

runners_data.name: La Trinite
runners_data.note: Improved four-year-old who ran second over 1m4f on Good last time out at OR 50, suggesting the handicapper may have caught up; a genuine rear-of-field operator by nature, though the steady pace set by Artavian works against the sharp late burst it will be looking for, and all five career runs have been on Good or better ground before today.

runners_data.name: Worlington
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for in-form George Boughey (7 wins from 40 over 14 days) who won over 1m4f on Good and placed twice at 1m on Standard — the step to 2m is the key unknown; Billy Loughnane's booking is notable, and a horse comfortable tracking a lone leader from a prominent position may find this race set up perfectly if the stamina holds.

runners_data.name: Smith
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran at OR 45 returning from a 49-day break and fitted with a visor; by nature a deep hold-up horse who has placed in handicaps at 2m on Standard before, but age, the layoff, and the likely lack of a true pace to chase all argue against a big run.

runners_data.name: Home Secretary
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed three-year-old from Sir Mark Prescott's yard, fitted with a visor and dropping back from two runs over 1m4f on Good ground; the step to 2m on AW for the first time is an unknown quantity, but Prescott horses at Lingfield are always worthy of respect and the low weight of 9st 1lb gives a physical edge if the stamina proves sufficient.

runners_data.name: Femme Fatale
runners_data.note: James Tate three-year-old fitted with a hood, stepping up considerably in trip from a best run of 1m4f on Soft; form of 649-85 is patchy and the AW debut adds further uncertainty, though at 127lbs she is well in at the weights if the trip and surface click — the evidence base is simply too thin to be confident.

runners_data.name: October Surprise
runners_data.note: Two-year-old — technically the youngest and lightest in the race at 117lbs — returning from a 221-day absence with a form string of 8698 exclusively at 1m on AW; the fades-in-finish flag, lack of any run beyond 1m, and extended layoff make this a very difficult proposition at 2m despite the low weight.

races.paceDynamic: Artavian is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m Lingfield AW trip on Standard ground. With eight of the remaining nine runners carrying hold-up profiles, the race is almost certain to develop as a single-file procession for much of the journey, with Artavian setting an honest but uncontested tempo that risks turning the final two furlongs into a bunched cavalry charge. The redistribution flag is significant here: Master Dancer, Break Point, La Trinite, Smith, and October Surprise are all genuine closers who have been pushed forward on the pace map simply because the field cannot accommodate that many hold-up horses at the rear — in practice, the rear of the field will be congested and those horses will race closer than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours a prominent racer or a horse with the tactical speed to track Artavian closely and pounce in the straight, rather than a deep closer who relies on a truly strong pace to generate the gaps needed from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Artavian Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian bowls along uncontested and sets a measured, even-tempo gallop that never truly tests the closers.
scenarios.body: Artavian dictates every yard at a pace entirely of its own choosing, and with no rival willing or able to apply pressure, it reaches the home straight with a comfortable lead and enough energy to hold on; the lack of a genuine pace battle means hold-up horses never get the strong gallop they need to unleash a decisive late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travels prominently just behind Artavian, conserves energy through the steady pace, and kicks past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third throughout exploits the generous tempo by never burning unnecessary energy, then produces a clean sustained finish as Artavian tires late; Worlington, on recent winning form over 1m4f-1m6f and ridden by Loughnane for the in-form Boughey yard, is best positioned to execute this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Rattle Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Artavian overcooks the early pace or the field bunches tightly enough to create a fast final quarter-mile that drags genuine hold-up types into contention.
scenarios.body: The compressed rear contingent, despite being redistributed on the map, includes Break Point — a proven stayer with a genuine win over 2m on Standard — and La Trinite, who rattled home for second last time on Good ground at 1m4f; if those horses can thread through traffic they can finish strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets at Weights
scenarios.trigger: If the handicapper has significantly overestimated the field and a lightly-weighted or unexposed runner finds the trip and pace perfectly suited.
scenarios.body: Home Secretary or Femme Fatale, both lightly raced three-year-olds unexposed at this distance who carry the lowest weights, could outrun their raw form figures if the even pace allows a stamina edge to show; their hold-up styles do not naturally suit this shape, but youth and unexposed stamina reserves give them a residual each-way chance.

watchPoints.text: Watch Artavian's early sectionals — if David Probert allows the gallop to become genuinely slow through the first mile, the race effectively becomes a sprint finish that could expose Artavian's modest recent form and open the door for any horse with tactical speed to cruise past.

Break Point is the most dangerous closer in the field given its proven 2m Standard win, but Jude Fernandes (7lb claimer) will need to navigate a congested rear group — watch for gaps opening down the Lingfield straight as the hold-up horses fan out.

Worlington's stamina at 2m is unproven after five runs at 1m-1m4f; if Boughey has the horse fit enough to see out the trip, the prominent-racing profile suits perfectly, but any sign of the horse tying up inside the final two furlongs would cost it dearly.

La Trinite has run all five career starts on Good or Good-to-Firm ground — today's Standard AW surface is a surface debut, and Dougie Costello will need to judge the horse's response to the all-weather very carefully from the back of the field.

Home Secretary's visor is fitted again after 5/12f/GOO last time; Sir Mark Prescott rarely runs horses without a clear plan at Lingfield, and a tongue-tied, visored three-year-old stepping sharply in trip for this yard merits monitoring in the betting market for any late move.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Counsel
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type with a course win on this exact surface and going combination; David Probert holds the book, and hg:t headgear should sharpen him — solid each-way profile if he gets a good position behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Lebron Power
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner, but his STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that he is broadly racing in role — the caution is that Hannon's horse has been campaigned over slightly longer trips and his five recent runs are mixed; Sean Levey will need to press for early lead without over-committing.

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this consistent six-year-old who places frequently but rarely wins — hg:p headgear applied, and his three recent runner-up finishes at similar going suggest he'll travel prominently, but his 0-for-15 conversion on Standard going caps optimism.

runners_data.name: Hoodie Hoo
runners_data.note: Strong recent form includes a second on this surface; Billy Loughnane rides, and his natural inclination is to race up with the pace — the issue is that with several genuine prominent types ahead of him in the queue, he may be forced to concede ground early that he won't get back over 5f.

runners_data.name: Sandscreendeliverd
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs takes a hold-up horse with three placed efforts in similar conditions; showed a sharp second at 5f here before and carries a light 128lbs — genuine each-way claims if the tempo is honest, though the nine-length deficit to the leader in her last run signals she needs things to go right.

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Has run exclusively on AW surfaces across 15 recent starts and clearly handles Standard going well (2W3P), but the 96-day absence is a question mark; his prominent style cannot be exercised freely in this field — William Cox will find him further back than he likes.

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's six-year-old arrives on the back of a recent Goodwood win over course and distance — Luke Morris rides a genuine hold-up type who is 1W2P on similar going with the highest OR in the race (87) and a course win on Standard suggesting he is the horse to beat on profile.

runners_data.name: Havana Blast
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's four-year-old is placed regularly on AW (1W3P on this going) and hg:t headgear is applied; Daniel Muscutt rides a prominent type who should get a clean run just behind the pace — a horse that could be dangerous if the leader tires.

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: Three wins from five recent starts including back-to-back victories last time, but the STA going record reads 0W0P from three starts — Joey Haynes rides a hold-up type who clearly relishes faster conditions and may find this surface blunting that finishing kick.

races.paceDynamic: Lebron Power is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push him from the gates on a flat 5f Lingfield AW surface, he should be able to stride into a comfortable lead and dictate a sustainable, metronomic pace. The field does contain more prominent-running types than positions allow — Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale are natural front-to-midpack horses who will find themselves shuffled into a midfield slot they don't naturally occupy, reducing their effectiveness and adding traffic risk. Nogo's Dream and Counsel will attempt to travel close to Lebron Power but are unlikely to pressurise him into a frantic opening, meaning the race is set to be run at an honest but not savage tempo. This shape — an uncontested front-runner controlling a steady pace on a flat track — most strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types with a powerful sustained finish, particularly hold-up horses like Michaela's Boy, Sandscreendeliverd, and Law Of Average who can close into a tempo that doesn't burn itself out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lebron Power Leads Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Lebron Power breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead, dictating a fair but sustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Lebron Power controls fractions from the front without pressure, and the race sets up as a one-run affair in the final furlong where horses with a powerful sustained finish can reel him in or hold their position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and prominent runners tie each other up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Michaela's Boy and Law Of Average, both genuine hold-up horses with recent winning form, get a clean run from off the pace and pick off the tiring prominent runners late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If Lebron Power or a close-tracking prominent horse finds enough to repel the closers in the dying strides.
scenarios.body: A steady early tempo means the front-runner or a horse like Counsel or Nogo's Dream, travelling well just behind, never fully exhausts its reserves and kicks clear before the closers arrive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go faster than expected and the early sections are run at a frantic clip, burning out those up with the pace.
scenarios.body: A rare scenario given Lebron Power's tendency to control rather than blaze, but if it unfolds, Sandscreendeliverd and Michaela's Boy benefit most as deep closers with course-and-distance form on this surface.

watchPoints.text: Michaela's Boy arrives as top-rated (OR 87) with a recent win and genuine hold-up credentials — watch whether Luke Morris gets a clean passage from off the pace, as any traffic issues would cost him dearly over 5f.

Hoodie Hoo and Dontspoilasale are both natural prominent types who cannot secure their preferred position in this field — watch if either horse over-races or gets squeezed out early, as frustration in the first furlong could ruin their race.

Law Of Average's AW/Standard going record is 0W0P from three attempts despite recent wins on Firm and Good — watch how Joey Haynes deploys him, as a hold-up horse with no AW form to show represents a genuine surface-reliability risk.

Lebron Power breaks from stall position — watch his gate reaction and the first two furlongs closely; if he is challenged for the lead by Counsel or Nogo's Dream, the tempo will rise and change the complexion of the entire race shape.

Dontspoilasale returns after 96 days off for Jim & Best — watch his early behaviour and whether he travels with his usual rhythm, as an absence of three months in a fast 5f contest can leave a horse flat in the critical opening stages.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Solar Edge
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old who has finished first or second in three of his last four starts including two on AW Standard, sits naturally prominent and should be covered up just off Temple Of Athena, making him the horse best positioned to benefit if the pace is honest without being brutal.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer with a strong AW Standard record (13 runs, 3 wins, 6 places) but has to overcome the congestion problem facing all closers here; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking but the horse has shown inconsistency (U in recent form) and 6f may be his sharper trip.

runners_data.name: Tan Rapido
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type whose true style means he will be shuffled to the rear end of a large chasing bunch; his recent form string (7-5-7-8-8) offers little encouragement for a tight race, and despite Standard going suiting (8 runs), the style mismatch in this shape is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Missile
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse mapped toward midfield through redistribution given the volume of closers, not through any front-running tendency; his best Standard-going form shows some competence (2W, 2P from 8 runs) but 64 days off the track and a field this compressed makes a winning run hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Nezeeh
runners_data.note: Overseas-trained hold-up type with alarming form figures (9-12-9-14-9) and only 2 from 15 Standard-going runs; squeezed into midfield here by default rather than design, and there is little in the record to suggest he can overcome both the positional difficulty and his poor recent returns.

runners_data.name: Mick's Spirit
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old but remarkably consistent on AW Standard (14 runs, 3W 4P), won at this course and distance and has headgear (tongue-tie/visor) to sharpen him up; trainer has no runners in the last 14 days (0/5) which is a minor concern, but the course-and-distance form makes him dangerous if he finds daylight.

runners_data.name: Dyrholaey
runners_data.note: Top-rated in the field at OR 87, five wins from 14 Standard-ground runs including course wins at 6f, and back after 77 days off with Archie Watson's yard 2/17 in the last fortnight suggesting racecourse readiness; the 5lb claimer Harry Vigors takes off useful weight, though stepping back to 5f from 6f home-track races may shorten his finishing window.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the race's sole pace-setter; won at OR 75 on Standard going (this course) last time and has the experience to control from the front at a measured tempo, but is up 12lbs on that winning mark and carries the highest weight assigned (139lbs) while rated joint-top — the style is ideal but the conditions ask questions.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been back in action just 14 days ago (the freshest horse in the race on that measure), placed twice from eight AW Standard runs and won at 5f on Good ground; Robert Cowell also saddles Ziggy's Missile, splitting yard focus, but Jack Mitchell is a strong pilot and Almaty Star has the class and fitness edge over several of the other closers.

races.paceDynamic: Temple Of Athena is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should settle into a controlled, uncontested rhythm from stall one on Lingfield's five-furlong AW straight. Solar Edge is the only other natural prominent-type and will likely slot into second, meaning the early fractions are set by one horse rather than a contested battle — this creates a sustainable, organised pace rather than a suicidal burn-up. The majority of the field — Tan Rapido, Ziggy's Missile, Nezeeh, Mick's Spirit, Dyrholaey and Almaty Star — are all hold-up types compressed into a midfield cluster, which means the closers will likely be racing in a bunch and must find room late rather than enjoying a clean, unimpeded run. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit close to the controlled pace or race prominently without overextending themselves early, as the hold-up brigade face a congestion problem and will have to produce their effort simultaneously; the field holds more hold-up types than the map can honestly accommodate at the rear, and Dyrholaey and Almaty Star are most likely to actually secure positions toward the front of that chasing pack given their class and recent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Athena Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Temple Of Athena sets a sustainable lead and holds on as the hold-up pack fails to find a clean run in time.
scenarios.body: Temple Of Athena dictates from flag to finish at a measured gallop on Standard AW ground, and Solar Edge, tucked in just off her shoulder, benefits most from the proximity to the pace with a clear passage. The congested hold-up group arrives too late to peg back horses who never lost momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Horse Picks Through
scenarios.trigger: If Dyrholaey threads through the congested midfield pack to deliver a decisive late challenge.
scenarios.body: Dyrholaey, the highest-rated horse in the field at OR 87 with strong AW course form and five wins from 14 Standard-ground runs, has the quality to pick through a bunched field if Temple Of Athena's early tempo is just hot enough to leave a gap. Harry Vigors's claim reduces the weight burden, and a horse who has won at 6f on this track can produce a powerful enough finish to nail the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pounce En Masse
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo proves too strong mid-race and the entire hold-up group converges simultaneously to swamp the pace-setters.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse or minor stumble from Temple Of Athena could compress the race and open a closing sprint that suits the deepest hold-up types, but given most of these closers are genuinely out of position and racing in a tight cluster, picking one clean winner from the group is extremely difficult. Almaty Star, with AW experience and a sharp recent return 14 days ago, and Mick's Spirit, who has four wins and four places from 14 Standard-going runs, are best-placed within this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Temple Of Athena over-speeds early and blows up before the final furlong, turning this into a scramble.
scenarios.body: Without the pace-setter maintaining her rhythm, the race devolves into a sprint from two furlongs out with no clear positional advantage, and the closers who find the clearest route will grab it. Accrual, who has strong AW Standard-going figures across 13 runs, and Ziggy's Missile, despite being a natural hold-up type mapped out of role, carry the profile for this outcome, though it is the least organised and most luck-dependent shape.

watchPoints.text: Temple Of Athena carries 139lbs at OR 87 after winning off OR 75 — watch whether Pierre-Louis Jamin allows her to coast or if the weight and rating hike cause her to tie up late, which would transform the outcome entirely.

The hold-up cluster of Tan Rapido, Ziggy's Missile, Nezeeh and Mick's Spirit will be racing in close quarters for the same midfield-to-rear territory — watch for crowding and checked runs in the final two furlongs, particularly near the inner rail.

Dyrholaey has been off 77 days and races over 5f rather than his recent 6f course trips — watch whether Harry Vigors positions him aggressively to offset any fitness or trip concern, as a tardy start from the back could make his task impossible.

Accrual shows a U (unseated) in recent form — watch his behaviour pre-race and whether Rossa Ryan opts to drop him in quietly to settle him, as any early anxiety could see him use up energy before the race begins.

Mick's Spirit has course-and-distance winning form and goes on this surface reliably (14/15), but Conrad Allen's trainer strike rate in the last 14 days is 0/5 — watch market moves in the final 30 minutes to gauge stable confidence.

races.name: Expert Entertainment & Event Solutions Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Follow attheraces On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Wild Rosie
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's filly has form at the 8f trip on Standard AW and has shown ability but placed form has dried up in recent runs; her hold-up style is genuine and she runs out of her natural position here given the crowded rear, with fading in finishes a concern that undermines her claims in a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: John Butler's 3yo holds multiple placed efforts at 8f on Standard AW — six runs at this trip and going combination producing three places — making her one of the better qualified horses in the field for this precise set of conditions; her true style is hold-up but she is pushed into midfield on the map due to the depth of closers, and she will need to travel forward enough to avoid being stranded.|

runners_data.name: Action Reaction
runners_data.note: George Boughey's colt has been finding only 6-8 rivals ahead of him in recent Flat handicaps and has failed to register a win or place on the AW at this class; he is a genuine hold-up type shown in midfield only because the rear of the map is congested, and his 44-day absence adds a fitness question.|

runners_data.name: Moravian
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 3yo has raced exclusively at shorter trips (5-7f) before this 1m assignment, making the step up in distance his primary question; a true hold-up racer mapped forward here out of necessity, his three-run form base on turf/AW gives little confidence he will see the mile out.|

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: Karen Jewell's charge has finished 8th or worse in four of his last five starts and carries a noted tendency to fade in the closing stages — a damaging trait in a race likely to compress into a sprint; he is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield on the map, and his trainer's 0 from 3 in the last 14 days suggests no strong yard momentum.|

runners_data.name: Laurasia
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan without a runner in 14 days and Georgia Dobie riding, Laurasia has placed twice in her last five but at a higher class level than the current OR=46 rating suggests she should be running; a true hold-up type shifted into midfield for the map, she brings modest AW form but lacks the proven Standard-going wins to be confident at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Ruiz
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's 3yo is a redistibuted prominent type placed on the lead solely because no confirmed front-runner exists in the race; his form figures of 0,0,6 in three recent Flat runs are deeply uninspiring and he fades in finishes, meaning his role as pace-setter is more circumstantial than authentic, and the race shape depends entirely on how much he commits to the lead.|

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: J S Moore's runner has the joint-highest OR in the race at 54 and returns just three days after his last run — a quick turnaround that could indicate fitness or trainer confidence; he is a genuine hold-up type whose 4th at 7f on Standard AW represents his best recent piece of form, and Taylor Fisher's 1-from-13 in 14 days suggests modest recent yard stats.|

runners_data.name: Whazzimo
runners_data.note: James Ferguson's 3yo has been running exclusively at 5-6f before this step up to a mile, making the distance question the most significant flag against him; he fades in finishes and his three runs all came on Good or better ground before today's Standard AW surface, so both the trip and the surface represent genuine unknowns — T14 of 4/8 is encouraging for yard form.|

runners_data.name: Athenian Spirit
runners_data.note: William Knight's horse arrives with four placed efforts in his last five runs including two 2nds at 7-8f on Standard AW, making him the most consistent place-getter in the field on this surface and trip combination; shown in midfield on the map as a redistributed hold-up type, his genuine tactical speed and proximity to the pace in prior races means he is among those best equipped to find a useful position from a congested rear.|

races.paceDynamic: Ruiz is the only horse mapped to the front but is a redistributed prominent type rather than a natural front-runner, meaning this 1m Lingfield AW contest is set to be run at a controlled, sustainable gallop with no horse genuinely committed to making it a test. With just one pace-setter and the remainder of the field comprised almost entirely of hold-up horses — many of them redistributed to midfield simply because the map cannot place them all at the rear — the race is likely to crawl early before a sprint develops in the straight. Horses racing closest to Ruiz off a slow tempo will hold a decisive positional advantage, as the closing ground from deep will be compressed and difficult to find. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or midfield types who are quick enough to respond to a sprint finish, and among those, the horses with genuine proximity to the pace and proven Standard-going form at this course are best placed; true closers arriving from well off the pace face an uphill task in a compressed finish. The field is overloaded with hold-up horses — Athenian Spirit, Fallacious Promise, Action Reaction, Moravian, Laurasia, and Henfield cannot all settle where they want, and those with the natural gate speed to push forward into midfield early, rather than being stranded last, are the ones most likely to secure a workable position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Tempo Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ruiz trots the field along at a steady gallop and the race turns into a 2f dash.
scenarios.body: Ruiz sets a moderate pace that keeps the field bunched, and the race develops into a sprint home from around the 2f pole; horses who have tracked in the first three to five lengths of the leader enter the straight with the decisive advantage. Horses with tactical speed and proven Standard-going form — particularly those who can sit handy off the compressed pace without needing a true test — are best suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and reward horses who travel powerfully through the race from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger gallop from Ruiz means the field spreads across the track by halfway, creating genuine stamina questions in the final furlong; horses who travel smoothly through midfield and quicken efficiently in the closing stages benefit most. Fallacious Promise, with multiple placed efforts at this course and trip, and Athenian Spirit, who has shown a consistent ability to finish into the places on Standard AW, are the profiles to follow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Ruiz controls the race unchallenged and kicks clear turning in without drawing a serious response.
scenarios.body: With no natural front-runner to pressurise Ruiz, he could dictate every yard and simply sprint clear off a slow pace before the hold-up horses can organise their challenge; the style-fit discount applies given his redistributed status, but the absence of any rival who will commit to racing prominently makes this outcome non-trivial. A horse who secures a clear lead and quickens without pressure in a field of reluctant hold-up types could prove very difficult to reel in over 1m on a tight track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and horses from the furthest back find the ground opening up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given that the majority of the field are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield — they are not genuine closers and will not be tracking far off the pace; a genuine late flourish from the back of the field depends on horses who are not naturally positioned to deliver it. Wild Rosie and Whazzimo, both flagged as fading types, represent further risk in this shape, making a textbook closing move the most scenario-dependent and low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Ruiz is the only horse on the lead but is a reluctant front-runner with a fading tendency — watch at the 3f pole to see if he capitulates suddenly, as any sharp deceleration will compress the finish and benefit the horses immediately behind him rather than those coming from further back.

Athenian Spirit and Fallacious Promise are both genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield — watch how much ground Hector Crouch and Luke Morris actually concede at the start, as both jockeys may push forward to avoid being buried, creating mid-race position battles that alter the race shape.

Whazzimo and Ernie McCrew are joint top-weight at OR=54 but both are stepping up significantly in trip from recent sprint form — watch whether either fades badly inside the final furlong, as a sudden weakening from the front-runners could leave the race to horses already positioned closer to the pace.

With seven of ten runners carrying some form of redistribution or style-fit caveat, the draw and early traffic are unusually important in this race — watch the first furlong to see which of the crowded hold-up brigade actually gets a clear passage and which is forced to switch or check, as that early decision will define the finish.
